title: Reduce GraphQL resolver contention via read-path slicing and response pipelining
creator: Miguel Santos
description: Observed sustained tail-latency regressions on the Console API over the last two quarters. Root causes identified: heavy GraphQL resolvers that synchronously fan out to multiple downstream services, duplicated cache keys across resolver layers causing cache churn, and a single merged response path that waits for all subtasks before returning (amplifying p99). This ticket scopes a targeted refactor: slice the read path into small parallel shards with bounded concurrency, introduce response pipelining to stream partial fields back to the client where safe, standardize memoization for idempotent resolver calls, and consolidate cache key shaping to reduce duplication. Goal is to reduce p99 latency and CPU tail pressure without changing API semantics for current clients.
acceptance_criteria: p99 latency for /graphql-console endpoint reduced to <= 300ms under 95th percentile load profile (baseline measured at ~860ms)
end-to-end CPU utilization on console-backend pods reduced by at least 20% during synthetic replay of customer traffic
no Semantic API changes: existing field ordering and payload contracts remain compatible
automated integration tests cover streaming partial responses and fallback to full-join path
Observability: per-field resolver latency histograms, cache-hit/miss breakdown, and a dashboard comparing before/after metrics
tech_notes: Introduce a ReadPathSlice abstraction: partition GraphQL selection sets into independent shards based on data dependency graph; execution uses Promise.allSettled-like concurrency with configurable shard parallelism (default 8)
Implement lightweight per-request memoization layer for resolver functions (TTL tied to request lifetime) to eliminate duplicate upstream calls within the same request
Standardize cache key canonicalization across resolver layers: use stable composite keys (resource_type:resource_id:field_set_hash) and evict on schema change events
Add response pipelining hook in HTTP layer that permits streaming of ETag-able partial sub-responses using chunked JSON lines; provide a flag to opt-out for legacy clients
Leverage DataLoader for batched DB/ upstream calls where entity fanouts exist; add instrumentation to ensure batching efficiency (batch sizes, wait windows)
Avoid blocking synchronous calls in hot resolvers; move slower enrichment calls to background enrichment with stale-while-revalidate where possible
Measure and expose per-resolver memory allocation and heap churn; add guardrails (max keys per-request memo cache, max shard concurrency) to prevent OOM under heavy load
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind console.feature.read_path_slicing. Staged rollout: 1) Enable in internal staging, run 72h synthetic replay; 2) Canary 5% of production traffic for 6h, observe p50/p95/p99 and error budget; 3) Ramp to 25% for 12h, then 100% if metrics stable. Provide immediate kill-switch via feature flag and fallback to legacy join path on increased error rate or disk pressure.
metrics_baseline: Baseline (2026-02-20 replay): p50=85ms p95=320ms p99=860ms; mean CPU per-pod=72%; median cache hit ratio=62%
current_status: Prototype implemented in feature branch (github.com/redwood-inference/console-backend/pull/8421). Unit tests added for shard executor and memoization. Integration harness includes replay script and a dashboard in Grafana (dashboards/console-readpath-compare). Running staging replay now.
blockers: Need infra quota bump for additional staging pods to run 72h replay (ticket INF-4812)
Finalize streaming contract with frontend team to avoid breaking client-side parsers
